classification.difficultyReason: Construct a general right-triangle diagram with complementary acute angles, express each tangent using the same two side lengths, and explain why exchanging opposite and adjacent produces reciprocal ratios.

content.prompt: Draw a diagram and explain why $\tan(90^\circ-\theta)=\frac1{\tan\theta}$.

answer.short: The opposite and adjacent sides exchange roles for complementary angles. If $\tan\theta=\frac ba$, then $\tan(90^\circ-\theta)=\frac ab=\frac1{\tan\theta}$.
answer.worked:
In the right-angled triangle, the acute angles are $\theta$ and $90^\circ-\theta$. Relative to $\theta$, opposite is $b$ and adjacent is $a$. Relative to $90^\circ-\theta$, opposite is $a$ and adjacent is $b$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac ba\\\tan(90^\circ-\theta)&=\frac ab\\\tan(90^\circ-\theta)&=\frac1{b/a}\\\tan(90^\circ-\theta)&=\frac1{\tan\theta}\end{align*}$$
